extracted.intended_audience: general NPR listeners/readers and those following media industry practices
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and reporting on the ethical use of AI, authorship verification, and editorial accountability in news articles and bylines. Focuses on standards news organizations should follow when using AI or contracting outside vendors for content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify authorship and identity of bylined writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Named authors should be real people; publishers must confirm that writers who appear in bylines actually exist and wrote the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report found authors (e.g., 'Drew Ortiz') who did not exist; Futurism discovered the author's photograph came from a database of AI-created images. Newsrooms should check author identities and the provenance of bio photos and not rely on unverified bylines to lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about use of AI in content creation
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should disclose when content is generated or substantially assisted by artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPR notes outlets are issuing holding policies/advisories saying AI is a tool to be used ethically and to enhance journalism, not to replace it. Publishers should clearly state whether AI was used to write or substantially edit an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human editorial review and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: All published content should undergo human editing and review to ensure coherence, accuracy, and journalistic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some articles in question 'make no sense' and 'do not sound like they're written by a human being' (examples: awkward insights about practicing volleyball). Robust human review should catch nonsensical or low-quality AI output before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor and contractor transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsourced content providers must be truthful about how content is produced and must allow editorial oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sports Illustrated's outside contractor AdVon allegedly assured SI that 'all the articles were written and edited by people.' News organizations should require clear assurances, audit rights, and take action (including severing contracts) if vendors misrepresent their processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of pseudonyms and protection of author privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of pen names or pseudonyms to protect author privacy may be permissible but should not be used to conceal AI-generated content or fake identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI said some writers used a 'pen- or pseudo-name' to protect privacy. That practice should not mask deceptive practices—publishers must ensure pseudonymous bylines correspond to real contributors and transparent editorial processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain trust and credibility with audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about AI and bylines should prioritize preserving reader trust and the credibility of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revelations that AI-generated content or fake authors were used can erode credibility and treat audiences 'simply as consumers and not as citizens.' Newsrooms should weigh job-displacement concerns and reputational harms when deploying AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement newsroom AI policies
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should create formal policies (holding policies/advisories) governing how AI is used across reporting, editing, and publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPR reports that 'serious news organizations' are issuing advisories to figure out how to use AI ethically. Policies should define permitted AI uses, required disclosures, and oversight mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear attribution and accountable public statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When allegations arise, organizations should issue clear, accountable statements explaining what happened and what steps will be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes SI/Arena's statement 'didn't answer a whole host of questions' and 'read a little bit as though it had been generated by artificial intelligence itself.' Public communications should be transparent, specific, and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit AI use to augmentation (research/analysis) rather than wholesale writing
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can be used for tasks like scouring databases and assisting reporters, but should not replace the core reporting and writing done by journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article distinguishes accepted uses—'scouring databases'—from problematic wholesale article generation. Use AI to enhance reporting workflows while keeping human judgement central to content creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify photos and multimedia provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the origin of photos and multimedia used for author bios or reporting to ensure they are not stock or AI-generated representations falsely presented as real persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Futurism found an author's photograph 'on a database of AI-created images meant to look like photographs of real people.' Newsrooms should verify image sources and metadata to avoid deceptive imagery.
